question.population: Adults, healthy or with risk factors (reviews limited to one illness count as partly)

decisions.reason: Beetroot juice vs placebo, but only in peripheral artery disease and outcomes are walking time and blood pressure, not FMD or artery stiffness.
Reports FMD and pulse wave velocity vs control, but the exposure is dietary nitrate in general; beetroot is not analysed on its own.
Placebo-controlled trials on endothelial function, but beetroot is pooled with inorganic nitrate supplements and not shown separately.

question.outcome: Thinking tests or blood flow in the brain

decisions.reason: Systematic review of beetroot juice in healthy adults and athletes that includes cognitive function outcomes; the abstract does not state a placebo comparison.

question.population: Adults, healthy or with risk factors (reviews limited to one illness count as partly)

decisions.reason: Systematically reviewed human trials of red beetroot products (various forms) on blood sugar in adults with different health conditions, including T2DM, obesity and hypertension.

question.outcome: Muscle soreness, damage markers or recovery of strength

decisions.reason: Measures heart and nervous-system recovery (heart rate variability, blood pressure) in postmenopausal women, not muscle soreness, damage markers or strength.
Pools placebo-controlled trials of beetroot juice in adults after exercise, measuring muscle function, soreness and damage markers.
Pools randomised trials comparing beetroot juice with placebo for creatine kinase, strength, jump height and muscle pain after damaging exercise.
Reviews beetroot studies with a placebo or control group, covering soreness, damage markers and strength recovery after muscle-damaging exercise.
Reviews nitrate intake in general, including beets, but the abstract does not analyse beetroot on its own and does not say whether a placebo was used.

question.population: Adults, healthy or with risk factors (reviews limited to one illness count as partly)
question.intervention: Beetroot juice or whole beetroot (nitrate-rich); reviews pooling nitrate salts count as partly
question.comparison: Nitrate-depleted juice, placebo or no beetroot

decisions.reason: It reviews sodium nitrate salts only and explicitly excludes beetroot juice studies, so beetroot is not the food examined.
Beetroot juice vs placebo/water/no intake on BP matches, but the population is limited to adults with hypertension.
It reviews beetroot extract supplementation in older adults only, a narrower population and possibly an extract rather than the whole food.
It pools dietary nitrate RCTs on BP without a separate beetroot juice analysis reported in the abstract.
Beetroot juice vs control on BP matches, but the population is limited to patients with arterial hypertension.
It pools inorganic nitrate RCTs on BP; beetroot juice is not analysed separately in the abstract.
Meta-analysis of RCTs of beetroot juice vs control groups, including nitrate-depleted juice, on resting SBP and DBP in humans.
Systematic review of RCTs of beetroot juice vs control on BP in healthy, pre-hypertensive and hypertensive people.
It mixes nitrate sources (beetroot juice, lozenges, diet) and is limited to adults with raised BP.
It pools inorganic nitrate and beetroot juice vs placebo on BP without a separate beetroot-only analysis in the abstract.

question.population: Healthy adults, from untrained to athletes
question.outcome: Endurance, time to exhaustion, time trials or oxygen uptake

decisions.reason: Beetroot vs comparison with VO2peak among outcomes, but limited to postmenopausal women and focused mainly on autonomic recovery.
Dietary nitrate, usually beetroot juice, on exercise capacity, but in people with chronic respiratory disease, not healthy adults.
Food-based nitrate (beetroot juice) on time to exhaustion in controlled trials, but limited to older adults.
Placebo-controlled nitrate trials with VO2max and a beetroot subgroup, but limited to athletes and pooled with nitrate salts.
Meta-analysis of beetroot juice on VO2max and exercise performance, with subgroups by athlete status.
Placebo-controlled trials of beetroot juice on VO2max/VO2peak in healthy adults, from recreational to trained.
Systematic review of beetroot juice on physical performance, including endurance, in healthy adults and athletes.
Umbrella review of beetroot juice on performance, including time to exhaustion and aerobic endurance, in athletes and healthy adults.
Outcomes are muscle strength, power and sprint in females, not endurance or oxygen uptake; nitrate also includes salts.
Outcome is exercise-induced muscle damage markers, not endurance performance or oxygen uptake.
Outcome is resistance exercise performance (squat, bench press), not endurance or oxygen uptake.
Endurance performance with nitrate-rich foods analysed as a group; beetroot juice is not clearly analysed on its own.
Randomised trials in healthy adults, with a separate beetroot juice subgroup showing effects on exercise performance.
Umbrella review of nitrate vs placebo on time to exhaustion and other outcomes, but beetroot juice is not analysed on its own.
Beetroot juice and sports performance, but it reviews beetroot combined with other supplements rather than vs placebo alone.
Placebo-controlled trials on VO2peak and time to exhaustion, with a separate subset of healthy people taking beetroot juice.
Dietary nitrate from mixed sources, and outcomes are muscular strength and endurance rather than whole-body endurance.
Nitrate vs placebo on endurance and VO2 in healthy adults, but beetroot juice is not analysed separately from other nitrate.
Beetroot-based supplements, but only in healthy males and with muscular endurance and strength outcomes.
Nitrate on endurance time-trial performance, but beetroot juice is not analysed separately from other nitrate sources.
Beetroot versus placebo, but only in combat sports athletes, and the outcomes are mostly muscle force and oxidative metabolism rather than endurance.

Placebo-controlled time trial and time-to-exhaustion pooling in healthy adults, but it pools all dietary nitrate sources with no separate beetroot analysis.
Looks at explosive efforts of 6 seconds or less (sprint and power), not endurance or oxygen uptake.
Looks at weightlifting (resistance exercise) performance, not endurance, time trials or oxygen uptake.
Pools time-to-exhaustion and time-trial results in healthy people, but mixes beetroot juice with sodium nitrate and does not analyse beetroot on its own.
Looks at short-duration, high-intensity sprint performance, not endurance or oxygen uptake.
Endurance outcomes, but covers nitrate supplements in general rather than beetroot specifically, and only trained endurance athletes in cyclic sports.
Time-trial performance across training levels, but covers dietary nitrates in general with no separate beetroot analysis.
Oxygen uptake against placebo in healthy people, but pools beetroot with nitrate salts and other vegetables rather than analysing beetroot juice on its own.
